adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the code updates attendees and sends calendar updates/emails for any booking found by `id` without checking `booking.endTime` against “now” or any booking status (e.g., cancelled/rejected). The diff shows `booking.endTime` is read to build `evt` and then `prisma.booking.update(...)`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)` are always executed after the permission check. Whether adding guests to past/cancelled bookings is forbidden is a product rule not shown in the diff, but the absence of such guards is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case concern.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler builds `EventManager` using the acting user (`ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Although the booking query includes `booking.user.credentials`, those organizer credentials are never used. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Server input schema accepts empty, unbounded, duplicate, and non-normalized guest arrays; only the client enforces uniqueness, so direct tRPC callers can create duplicate attendee rows and trigger unbounded email/calendar fan-out

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so the carefully named filtered variable is bypassed and existing/blacklisted emails are treated as "new guests" in email routing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (whose email is attacker-controlled at public booking time) can add arbitrary guests, turning the app into an email/calendar-invite spam relay sent from the platform's sender domain.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any authenticated attendee of the booking to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the access check only forbids when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. That means any attendee can call `addGuests` and supply arbitrary `guests` emails (no count limit, only format + blacklist), which then triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, effectively allowing an attendee to cause the system to send calendar/email invites to arbitrary third parties from the platform/organizer context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no max length and handler has no rate limiting, allowing a single request to insert unbounded attendees and fan out mass emails.

Nothing in the diff shows any per-request size cap or rate limiting in this handler/router path, so a single request can add an arbitrarily large number of attendees and trigger a large outbound email burst (DoS/spam risk) introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Add-guest emails go to every attendee and replyTo lists all attendee emails, ignoring seatsShowAttendees and leaking other seat holders' emails in seated events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Attendee de-duplication is case-sensitive and guests input is not deduplicated, so the same address can be added repeatedly to spam or bloat a booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guests.filter(...)` comparing `guest === attendee.email` and checking `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing case, so `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com` won’t be treated as duplicates. Additionally, the server-side schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) does not enforce uniqueness and the handler never deduplicates `guests` itself, so a caller can submit duplicate addresses in `guests` and they will all be passed to `createMany`, potentially creating repeated attendee rows (or at minimum causing DB errors) and enabling spam/bloat. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner uses AND, so team admins who are not owners get denied, which fails closed but breaks the intended permission model.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The variable name and typical permission model imply it should allow either role (OR). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — No tests for case sensitivity: existing-attendee and blacklist checks compare raw guest casing against lowercased or stored emails, so mixed-case duplicates or blacklisted guests get through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Server schema and handler never dedupe guests within one request, and no test covers duplicate input creating duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as an array of emails and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the same `guests` array. Those duplicates are then passed to `createMany` (`guestsFullDetails`), which can create duplicate attendee rows (or cause a DB error) and can also trigger duplicate/incorrect email sending (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the original non-deduped `guests`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Emails go to raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, so existing or blacklisted addresses get "scheduled" emails, and no test checks the recipient list.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guests are filtered into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only `uniqueGuests` are persisted, but the email call uses the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the attendee email type is chosen via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`—so if the caller includes an email that was already an attendee, that existing attendee will be treated as a “new guest” and get the wrong (scheduled) email. (Blacklisted emails won’t be in `evt.attendees`, so they won’t receive emails, but the existing-attendee misclassification is a real defect.)
